title: Picking the ramp angles from real surf maps
caption: Every surf face in 41 local KSF maps: 51 degrees is by far the most common, so Surf Ramp uses a 5:4 slope (51.3 degrees); Steep Surf Ramp uses 2:1 (63.4 degrees). A 1x1 45-degree wedge would be walkable ground in Source, not a surf ramp.

title: How blocks join into one ramp
caption: Each ramp block stores its cut of a shared plane, so blocks placed next to each other continue the same slope at any size. The geometry (RampCell) is tested for exact plane continuity across neighbours.

title: First ramp textures
caption: The blocks agent drew two 16x16 textures in code (no fal key): cool teal for the 51-degree Surf Ramp, amber for the 63-degree Steep Surf Ramp, with a lit top/left edge to fit Minecraft's pixel style.

title: First in-game render
caption: The client game test builds a showcase in a superflat world: a joined 51-degree Surf Ramp (teal) backed by a 63-degree Steep Surf Ramp (amber), plus single blocks of each in all four facings. Slopes render as exact geometry, not stair steps.

title: Smooth slope up close, items in the hotbar
caption: Up close, the blocks join into one continuous slope with the texture lined up across cells. The hotbar shows both ramp items as wedges.

title: Java physics vs the real CS:S server
caption: The physics port replays a recording from a real Counter-Strike: Source server on surf_kitsune's ramp: same inputs, same ramp, worst difference 0.006 units over 100 ticks (tolerance 0.05). 18 engine recordings pass this way.

title: The 63-degree Steep Surf Ramp
caption: The 2:1 side of the showcase: eight blocks long and six tall, one smooth plane with a continuous grid.

title: One block of each type, in every facing
caption: Single ramp blocks facing north, east, south and west. Behind them, the cross-section of the joined showcase: a 51-degree side and a 63-degree side meeting at the ridge.

title: First surf in game
caption: The CS:S movement core now drives the player in Minecraft: dropped onto a 51-degree ramp at 788 units/s while holding the strafe key into the slope, the player glides along it. The speedometer above the hotbar shows horizontal speed in units/s.

title: The Karambit
caption: SurfCraft's surf-building tool: a 16x16 CS:GO-style karambit drawn in code, with a claw blade in a Fade finish (gold, purple, pink), a black grip and a finger ring. Zoomed, at 1x to 8x, and in hand next to the hotbar.

title: Getting the sprite to read as a karambit
caption: Before and after: the first tries drew a flat arc with a 1-pixel ring. The final sprite has a hooked claw blade with a dark outline (like vanilla swords) and a ring with a clear hole.

title: Copy a ramp chunk, extend it three times
caption: Sneak + right-click copies a hand-built 63-degree chunk (6x6x4, 96 blocks) onto the knife. Three right-clicks on the ramp put a copy after its end each time: 16 blocks long, every cell on the same slope plane.
